If I had more time to prepare and time for trial and error (In this case the clouds forced me to set up and snap within a few minutes), I would probably try a shorter exposure with higher ISO.

There are the usual tips: Aperture should be open. On a crop sensor your maximum exposure time should be (300 divided by your focal length) to avoid star trails. Bump the ISO as needed. I'd say the most important thing is to get a decently stable tripod and turn off vibration reduction/image stabilization. Use timed shutter (Start timer, step away from the camera) or a remote to avoid vibrations.
